hosting.//: Marketing site (Next.js, static-exported). 2026-05-28 — switched from frameworksBackend (Cloud Functions SSR) to pure static. firebase-frameworks' npm-ci-against-pnpm-lockfile pipeline kept breaking Cloud Build. Static export of Next.js 16 produces clean HTML/JS that Firebase Hosting serves at the edge. Deploy: `pnpm --dir marketing-site build && firebase deploy --only hosting:superwizor`.

redirects.//: /login is a real page on the marketing origin as of 2026-05-29 (src/app/[locale]/login/page.tsx). Bare /login (no locale prefix) gets the standard PL-default 307 to /pl/login/; the prefixed routes /pl/login/ and /en/login/ are served as static HTML and don't need redirects. The previous cross-origin redirect to the Flutter app is gone — the new LoginForm signs the user in on this origin, then routes by role.

PL default locale redirect. Next.js was configured with `localePrefix: 'as-needed'` so during SSR/dev the PL pages served at no-prefix paths (e.g. /register/therapist) and only EN got the /en prefix. Static export bakes both into explicit directories (out/pl/... and out/en/...); the proxy middleware that stripped the prefix at request time is gone. The redirects below restore the UX — every top-level no-prefix path forwards to its /pl/ equivalent. Result: visitors get the same UX as before — a quick 307 bounce, then a stable /pl/* URL.

Top-level no-prefix paths -> /pl/<same>. One redirect per top-level segment because Firebase Hosting source patterns are anchored: a single catchall would also match /pl/* and /en/* and create a loop. The :rest* capture preserves the deep path so /register/therapist/finish?token=x lands on /pl/register/therapist/finish?token=x.
Org-manager panel (docs/38). Same PL-default bounce as every other no-prefix path — the magic-link flow and docs reference bare /org.

Bare /admin needs its own exact-match peer because Firebase Hosting's :rest* requires at least one segment after the slash — `/admin` alone doesn't match `/admin/:rest*`. Same for /register, but most users land on a deeper register path.

rewrites.//: Stripe Checkout Session — browser POST from registration + upgrade flows. Served by billing-svc on Cloud Run (replaces broken Next.js API route which returned 404 on static export).
Stripe Billing Portal — browser POST from /account Subskrypcja card. Same migration rationale as /api/checkout.
NIP (Polish tax ID) lookup — browser GET from /account VAT form. Proxied by identity-svc (domain purity: NIP is an org data concern).

Admin org-detail catch-all. Static export can't pre-render every /admin/orgs/<id> because the IDs aren't known at build time. We ship a single template per locale (out/{pl,en}/admin/orgs/[id]/index.html — literal bracketed directory) and rewrite all matching /admin/orgs/<id> traffic to it. The client component reads usePathname() at runtime and fetches the matching org via AdminGetOrganization.

headers.//: Long-lived cache for hashed Next.js bundles
Cache images/fonts for 1 year (content-addressed or rarely changed)
Short cache for HTML pages so deploys propagate quickly. 5 min is enough for CDN benefit while keeping deploy-to-live latency low.

hosting.//: Flutter Web bundle (therapist + org-admin consoles). Deploy: `firebase deploy --only hosting:superwizor-app`.

headers.//: Entry points must ALWAYS revalidate so a deploy propagates immediately. Without this the browser caches index.html + flutter_service_worker.js and the service worker keeps serving a stale main.dart.js — i.e. 'the page won't refresh'. Hashed canvaskit/wasm/assets keep Firebase's default caching.
Bare root request (/) serves index.html — revalidate it too.
